candidates.citation_sentence: This experiment is similar to what was reported in Figure 2 of Castellarin et al. (2012).
candidates.notes: The replication found a statistically significant effect in the same direction (p = 0.032) but with a much smaller effect size (r = 0.24 vs r = 0.45) and substantial data quality concerns (non-detects, non-specific amplification). The authors do not explicitly claim success or failure. The replication found a statistically significant effect in the same direction (p = 0.032) but with a much smaller effect size than the original (median fold change 1.13 vs 3.15). The authors express substantial validity concerns regarding non-detects, high Ct values, and non-specific amplification, which undermines confidence in the replication result. A second coder could plausibly classify this as success given the significant p-value in the same direction.
